standards_source_doc: TN World History & Geography — Instructional Guide + TN State Standards (2025–2026)

social_studies_practices.text: Collect data and information from a variety of primary and secondary sources.
Critically examine primary or secondary sources.
Synthesize data from a variety of sources.
Construct and communicate arguments citing supporting evidence.

units.title: Imperialism in Asia and Latin America
Creation of New States and Decolonization

standards.title: Describe the concept of the divine right of kings as well as the features
standards.standard: Describe the concept of the divine right of kings as well as the features, strengths, and weaknesses of European absolutism, including Louis XIV, Versailles, and Peter the Great. (C, H, P)
ican: Describe the concept of the divine right and absolute monarchy using examples.
Describe the features, strengths, and weaknesses of absolute monarchy using evidence.
Compare the reigns of Louis XIV at Versailles and Peter the Great in Russia.

standards.title: Compare documents that establish limits on government in response to absolute monarchy (e
standards.standard: Compare documents that establish limits on government in response to absolute monarchy (e.g., the Magna Carta and the English Bill of Rights). (H, P)
ican: Compare the Magna Carta and English Bill of Rights and discuss how these documents established limits to create a constitutional monarchy.
Compare the constitutional monarchy in England with other absolute monarchies across continental Europe.

standards.title: Compare the major ideas of philosophers during the Age of Enlightenment
standards.standard: Compare the major ideas of philosophers during the Age of Enlightenment, such as Charles-Louis de Montesquieu, Thomas Hobbes, John Locke, and Jean-Jacques Rousseau. (C, E, H, P)
ican: Identify the causes of the Enlightenment, including emphasis on human reasoning.
Compare the major ideas of philosophers described in the following works:
Charles-Louis de Montesquieu’s The Spirit of the Laws
Thomas Hobbes’ Leviathan
John Locke’s Second Treatise of Government
Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s The Social Contract
Honors: Mary Wollstonecraft’s A Vindication of the Rights of Woman.

standards.title: Examine the causes and consequences of the English Civil War
standards.standard: Examine the causes and consequences of the English Civil War. (C, G, H, P)
ican: Describe the causes and identify the key people and their role in the civil war including:
James I and Charles I
Oliver Cromwell
Charles II
Identify the consequences of the conflict and the role of key people in the creation of England’s constitutional monarchy, including:
William and Mary
James II

standards.title: Identify how the ideas of the Enlightenment inspired Thomas Jefferson and the Declaration
standards.standard: Identify how the ideas of the Enlightenment inspired Thomas Jefferson and the Declaration of Independence. (C, G, H, P)
ican: Identify how the ideas of the Enlightenment inspired Thomas Jefferson and the Declaration of Independence.

standards.title: Identify the major causes of the French Revolution
standards.standard:
Identify the major causes of the French Revolution, including the impact of: (C, E, G, H, P)
The American Revolution 
conflicting social classes
economic factors 
enlightenment political thought
government corruption and weakness
ican: Describe the growing tensions between the Three Estates.
Define bourgeoisie and describe their growing political, social and financial resentments.
Identify economic causes of the French Revolution including:
lavish government spending
inflation
rapidly growing national debt
the tax burden of the Third Estate
Identify how the American Revolution contributed to rising debt and provided inspiration to the Third Estate.
Identify the impact of enlightenment political thought on the French Revolution, including:
Rousseau’s idea of social contract
Locke’s ideas equality and natural rights
Identify how government corruption, incompetence, and increasing weakness contributed to growing frustrations.

standards.title: Summarize the major events of the French Revolution (e
standards.standard: Summarize the major events of the French Revolution (e.g., storming of the Bastille, execution of Louis XVI, reign of terror), and trace the evolution of France’s government from constitutional monarchy to democratic despotism to the Napoleonic Empire. (C, E, G, H, P)
ican: Describe the role of each person in the Revolution:
Louis XVI
Marie Antoinette
Maximilien de Robespierre
Summarize and explain the connections between the major events of the French Revolution, including:
the Tennis Court Oath
the creation of the National Assembly
execution of Louis XIV
storming of the Bastille
Describe the Reign of Terror including:
Committee of Public Safety and Maximilien de Robespierre
National Convention
The Directory
Trace the evolution of France’s government from a constitutional monarchy to democratic despotism to the Napoleonic Empire and give reasons for this progression.

standards.title: Analyze the geographic
standards.standard: Analyze the geographic, political, and social factors that contributed to the rise and fall of Napoleon Bonaparte’s empire. (C, G, H, P)
ican: Analyze how geographic, political, and social factors created challenges within Napoleon’s empire and led to his fall, including the Continental System.

standards.title: Compare the American Revolution with the French Revolution
standards.standard: Compare the American Revolution with the French Revolution. (C, G, H, P)
ican: Compare the outcomes of the American Revolution with the French Revolution.
Honors: Compare the influential documents from both the American and French Revolutions.

standards.title: Explain the effects of the French Revolution on Europe and the world
standards.standard: Explain the effects of the French Revolution on Europe and the world, including the influence of: the Napoleonic Code, Concert of Europe, and Haitian Revolution. (C, G, H, P)
ican: Explain the effects of the Napoleonic Code.
Identify the political, economic, and social effects of the French Revolution on Europe.
Identify the cause and purpose of the Concert of Europe.
Compare the map of Europe before and after the Congress of Vienna in 1815.
Explain the effects of the French Revolution on Latin American Revolutions, specifically other revolutions throughout the world, including the Haitian Revolution, and the Mexican Revolution.

standards.title: Explain how the Agricultural Revolution
standards.standard:
Explain how the Agricultural Revolution, mechanization, and the “enclosure movement” led to rapid population growth, rural to urban migration, and the growth of major cities in Europe and North America. 
(C, E, G, H, P)
ican: Describe the Second Agricultural Revolution, including mechanization and the “enclosure movement.”
Explain how the Agricultural Revolution led to:
rapid population growth
rural to urban migration
the growth of major cities in Europe and North America.

standards.title: Explain the geographic and economic reasons why the Industrial Revolution began in England
standards.standard: Explain the geographic and economic reasons why the Industrial Revolution began in England, including: natural resources, entrepreneurship, labor, and access to capital. (E, G, H)
ican: Explain the geographic and economic reasons why the Industrial Revolution began in England, including:
natural resources
entrepreneurship
labor
access to capital

standards.title: Analyze how geographic and cultural features were an advantage or disadvantage to the diff
standards.standard: Analyze how geographic and cultural features were an advantage or disadvantage to the diffusion of the Industrial Revolution. (C, G, H)
ican: Analyze how geography differences aided or inhibited the diffusion of the Industrial Revolution.
Proximity to origin points of the Industrial Revolution
Availability of fuels and other raw materials
Analyze how cultural differences aided or inhibited the diffusion of the Industrial Revolution.
Entrepreneurship
Adherence to traditional methods of production

standards.title: Describe the geographic scale
standards.standard: Describe the geographic scale, trade routes, and conditions of the forced migration of Africans to the Western Hemisphere, including connections between slave labor and the growth of industrial economies. (C, E, G, H, P)
ican: Describe the geographic scale and trade routes of the forced migration of Africans to the Western Hemisphere.
Describe the connections between slave labor and the growth of industrial economies.especially through the textile industry.
Describe the cultural impact in both Africa and the Americas.

standards.title: Explain how scientific and technological innovations (e
standards.standard: Explain how scientific and technological innovations (e.g., the steam engine, new textile technology, steel processing, medical advances, electricity, and new methods of transportation) led to massive social, economic, cultural, and demographic changes. (C, E, G, H, P)
ican: Name and describe the major science and technological innovations, including:
steam engine
steel processing
electricity
new textile machines
medical advances (e.g., vaccines, microorganisms)
new methods of transportation
Explain how the scientific and technological innovations led to massive social, economic, cultural, and demographic changes.

standards.title: Evaluate the industrialization of Europe in terms of
standards.standard:
Evaluate the industrialization of Europe in terms of: 
Social benefits (e.g., increases in productivity and life expectancy) 
Social costs (e.g., harsh working and living conditions, pollution, child labor, and income inequality) 
Attempts to address these costs (e.g., political reform, urban planning, philanthropy, labor unionism, education reform, and public health and sanitation) 
(C, E, G, H, P)
ican: Evaluate the social benefits of industrialization, including:
increased productivity
improved life expectancy
Evaluate the social costs of industrialization, including:
harsh working and living conditions
pollution
child labor
income inequality
Evaluate the attempts to address the costs of the Industrial Revolution, including:
political reforms
labor unions
education reforms
urban planning
philanthropy
Public health and sanitation

standards.title: Compare and contrast the rise of the following economic theories as a result of industrial
standards.standard:
Compare and contrast the rise of the following economic theories as a result of industrialization: capitalism, communism, and socialism. 
(C, E, H, P)
ican: Compare and contrast the rise of the following economic theories because of industrialization: capitalism, communism, and socialism including:
basic definitions
proponents (Adam Smith and Karl Marx)
role of the individuals/community
distribution of Wealth
role of the Government

standards.title: Define nationalism
standards.standard: Define nationalism, and explain how nationalism, cultural geography, and physical geography contributed to the unification of nations, such as Germany and Italy. (C, G, H, P)
ican: Define nationalism.
Identify the role of each nationalist leader, including:
Otto von Bismarck
Giuseppe Mazzini
Camillo di Cavour
Giuseppe Garibaldi
Explain the growth of nationalism across Europe during the early 19th century.
Explain how nationalism, cultural geography, and physical geography contributed to the unification of Germany and Italy.

standards.title: Describe the rise of anti-Semitism in Europe during this time period
standards.standard: Describe the rise of anti-Semitism in Europe during this time period. (C, G, H, P)
ican: Describe the rise of anti-Semitism in Europe during this era including the Dreyfus Affair, Zionism, influence of heads of state.
Locate the Jewish Diaspora in this time period on a world map.

standards.title: Define imperialism
standards.standard:
Define imperialism, and analyze reasons for 19th century imperialism, including: (C, E, G, H, P)
competition between empires 
cultural justifications
the search for natural resources and new markets in response to rapid industrialization
ican: Define imperialism.
Analyze the main reasons for 19th century imperialism, including:
competition between empires for industrial resources
cultural justifications (e.g. Social Darwinism and The White Man’s Burden)
the search for natural resources and new markets in response to rapid industrialization

standards.title: Describe the natural resources and geographic features of Africa
standards.standard: Describe the natural resources and geographic features of Africa, their role in attracting European economic interests, and their impact on global trade. (C, E, G, H, P)
ican: Identify how natural resources and geographic features of Africa differ across the continent (e.g. oil, gold, iron, rubber, ivory, diamonds).
Explain the role of resources and geographic features in attracting European economic interests & the impact on global trade.

standards.title: Analyze the outcomes of the Berlin Conference and the impact of superimposed boundaries on
standards.standard: Analyze the outcomes of the Berlin Conference and the impact of superimposed boundaries on African Indigenous populations and compare the geographic progression of imperialistic claims on the African continent by European empires. (C, E, G, H, P)
ican: Analyze the outcomes and impact of the Berlin Conference, including:
colonization of different regions
differences in how European leaders approached colonies
effects of power structures
Explain the social and political impact of superimposed boundaries on Africa’s indigenous populations.
Compare the geographic progression of imperialistic claims on the African continent by European empires.

standards.title: Describe successful (e
standards.standard: Describe successful (e.g., Ethiopia) and unsuccessful (e.g., Zulu Wars and Ashanti Wars) examples of African resistance to European imperialism. (C, G, H, P)
ican: Describe successful examples of African resistance to European imperialism, including Ethiopian resistance.
Describe unsuccessful attempts to resist European imperialism, including the Zulu Wars and Ashanti Wars.

standards.title: Describe the importance of India to the British Empire
standards.standard: Describe the importance of India to the British Empire, the Suez Canal as a connection between Great Britain and India, and India’s reaction to British rule. (C, E, G, H, P)
ican: Describe the political, cultural, and economic structures in India before European Imperialism.
Describe the importance of India to the British Empire.
Name and describe the Suez Canal as a connection between the United Kingdom and India.
Explain India’s reaction to British rule, including the Sepoy Mutiny.

standards.title: Explain the growing influence of western powers on China from the Opium Wars through the B

standards.title: Describe the natural resources and geographic features of Central and South America
standards.standard: Describe the natural resources and geographic features of Central and South America, their role in attracting American and European economic interests, and their impact on global trade. (C, E, G, H, P)
ican: Describe the natural resources and geographic features of Central and South America, such as:
climates for plantation crops (i.e., bananas, coffee, sugar)
Isthmus of Panama as a location for a canal

standards.title: Describe how trench warfare
standards.standard: Describe how trench warfare, the resulting stalemate, war of attrition, and advances in weaponry (e.g., chemical weapons, machine guns, submarines, tanks) affected the course and outcome of World War I. (C, E, G, H, P)
ican: Describe trench warfare, the resulting stalemate, and the advances in weaponry, including the introduction of:
chemical weapons
submarines
machine guns
tank

standards.title: Analyze the importance of geographic factors in military decision-making and determine the
standards.standard: Analyze the importance of geographic factors in military decision-making and determine the principal theaters and significance of major battles in World War I (e.g., Battles of the Marne, Verdun, the Somme, etc.). (G, H, P)
